mainTopic: The rabbinic decrees that disqualify תרומה: the order of the decrees on hands, testing טבול יום and the liquid decrees, and who first decreed impurity on hands (שמאי והלל, their students, or שלמה).
overview: The גמרא goes through the list of things the רבנן decreed would make תרומה unfit, and it tests each item. First it settles the order of the decrees on hands: the decree on hands that touched a ספר תורה came first, and later it was extended to all hands. טבול יום is already impure מדאורייתא, so the גמרא deletes it from the list. Foods made impure by liquids means liquids made impure by hands, a decree made because of liquids made impure by a שרץ. Vessels made impure by liquids means liquids made impure by a שרץ, a decree made because of the liquids of a זב. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה credits the students of שמאי והלל with the decree on hands, when a ברייתא says שמאי והלל made it themselves. After rejecting two answers, it concludes that the masters decreed it but the people did not accept it, and the students decreed it again and the people accepted it. Finally it asks how this fits with a teaching that שלמה המלך already instituted washing hands. The answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the general hands decree came first, why have a separate one for a ספר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges an order of events in which the רבנן first decreed impurity on all hands. In that order, the separate decree on hands that touched a ספר תורה would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since this decree (on all hands) was made first, why do I need that one (on hands touching a ספר) as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its discussion of the decree that hands make תרומה unfit. It objects that if the decree on all hands came first, a special decree for hands touching a ספר would serve no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once every hand is already considered impure, a hand that touched a ספר is impure anyway. A second, narrower decree would add nothing. So the order in which the two decrees were made must be different.

keyTerms.meaning: they decreed
first, at the beginning
further, additionally
why do I need it? (signals that something seems superfluous)

steps.confusionAlert: The word הָךְ ("this one") points to a DIFFERENT decree in the question than in the answer. In this question, הָךְ means the general decree on all hands, and הָא means the ספר decree. In the answer (next step), הָךְ means the ספר decree.

phrases.english: Since this one (the decree on all hands) was decreed first
why do I need this one (the decree on hands touching a Sefer) in addition?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּהָךְ גְּזוּר בְּרֵישָׁא, הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of why hands disqualify תרומה, including the decree on hands that touched a ספר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the decree on all hands preceded the decree on hands that touched a ספר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A narrower decree made after a broader one that already covers it is superfluous.

steps.title: The ספר decree came first, then the decree on all hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the order. First the רבנן decreed on hands that touched a ספר, and later they extended the decree to all hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this one (the ספר decree) was made first, and afterward they decreed on all hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by flipping the order of the two decrees. The narrow decree came first, and the broad one came later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ספר decree was made, it was not superfluous, because no general hands decree existed yet. Later the רבנן widened it to cover all hands. This explains why both decrees are recorded.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces the corrected view)
and afterward, and then again
hands (here: the rabbinic impurity of hands)

steps.whatToRemember: The decree on hands was made in two stages. First came hands that touched a ספר תורה, and then all hands.

phrases.english: Rather, this one (hands touching a Sefer) was decreed first
and then they decreed on all hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָךְ גְּזוּר בְּרֵישָׁא, וַהֲדַר גְּזוּר בְּכוּלְּהוּ יָדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 1 by reversing the order of the decrees.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reordering the chronology of the decrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general decree on all hands came first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ספר decree came first, and it was later extended to all hands.

steps.title: טבול יום is already Torah law, so why is it listed as a decree?
steps.stepSummary: The list of rabbinic decrees includes טבול יום. But a טבול יום already disqualifies תרומה by Torah law, based on the פסוק "ובא השמש וטהר".
steps.simpleTranslation: And טבול יום? A טבול יום is a Torah-level matter, as it is written: "And the sun sets and he is pure."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the list, טבול יום. It objects that this one does not belong on a list of rabbinic decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that the person becomes pure only once the sun sets. So before sunset he is still impure for תרומה מדאורייתא. A rabbinic decree is not needed for something the תורה itself already forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who immersed today but must wait for sunset to be fully pure
from Torah law
as it is written
the portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be eaten in purity

phrases.english: And the one who immersed that day
a tevul yom is a Torah-law matter
as it is written: "And the sun sets and he is pure"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the list of decrees.
steps.kashyaTarget: Including טבול יום in the list of rabbinic decrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something already forbidden מדאורייתא cannot be counted as a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Remove טבול יום from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge and deletes טבול יום from the list of decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply agrees and says to take טבול יום off the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No clever answer is given here. The item is just removed, because it is Torah law and not a rabbinic decree.

keyTerms.meaning: remove from here; delete this item from the text

phrases.english: Delete tevul yom from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the קשיא of step 3 by emending the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: deleting the item from the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: טבול יום is one of the rabbinic decrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: טבול יום does not belong on the list, since it is Torah law.

steps.title: Foods made impure by liquids: which liquids?
steps.stepSummary: The list includes foods that became impure through liquids. The גמרא asks what made those liquids impure in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And foods that became impure through liquids: liquids made impure by what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next item on the list. It asks a clarifying question to pin down the exact case. The answer will come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether this case is Torah law or rabbinic depends on what made the liquid impure. So the גמרא needs to identify the source before it can call the case a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: foods
liquids
of what? (from what source?)

phrases.english: And the foods that became impure through liquids
through liquids made impure by what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source of impurity made the liquids impure in this case.

steps.title: Not liquids made impure by a שרץ, since that is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the case means liquids made impure by a שרץ. Foods made impure by such liquids are already impure מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means liquids made impure by a שרץ, those are Torah law, as it is written: "And any liquid that is drunk..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and rules it out. Liquids made impure by a שרץ already make food impure by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a שרץ teaches that liquids become impure and pass that impurity on. So that case needs no decree. The list must be talking about a different kind of liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (proposes an option that will be rejected)
a creeping creature whose carcass is a source of Torah-level impurity
because of, by means of
they are

phrases.english: If you say: through liquids that became impure because of a creeping creature
those are Torah law
as it is written: "And any liquid that is drunk" (shall be impure).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible answer to the question in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the case as שרץ-liquids.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already Torah law, so it cannot be a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: It means liquids made impure by hands, decreed because of שרץ-liquids
steps.stepSummary: The case is liquids made impure by hands, which are impure only מדרבנן. The רבנן made foods touched by these liquids impure, because they resemble liquids made impure by a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means liquids made impure by hands. This is a decree because of liquids made impure by a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer. The list means liquids that became impure through impure hands. The decree was made so that people would not confuse these with Torah-level שרץ-liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impurity of hands is itself rabbinic, so liquids they touch are only rabbinically impure. The רבנן still let those liquids make food impure, so that people would treat all impure liquids alike. This makes it a true rabbinic decree.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree
because of, on account of

phrases.english: Rather, through liquids that became impure because of hands,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ.
phrases.english: and it is a decree on account of liquids made impure because of a creeping creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer to the question in step 5, after step 6 ruled out שרץ-liquids.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liquids made impure by hands, decreed because of שרץ-liquids.

steps.title: Vessels made impure by liquids: which liquids?
steps.stepSummary: The list includes vessels that became impure through liquids. The גמרא asks what made those liquids impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And vessels that became impure through liquids: vessels made impure by liquids made impure by what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last item here and asks the same kind of clarifying question as before. It is setting up a test of possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, whether this case is Torah law or rabbinic depends on the source of the liquid's impurity. The גמרא follows the same pattern it used for foods.

keyTerms.meaning: vessels, utensils
became impure

phrases.english: And the vessels that became impure through liquids
vessels that became impure through liquids made impure by what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item, using the same pattern as step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source of impurity made the liquids that made the vessels impure.

steps.title: Not liquids of a זב, since those make vessels impure by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the case means liquids of a זב, such as spit. Those make vessels impure מדאורייתא, as derived from "וכי ירוק הזב בטהור".
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means liquids of a זב, those are Torah law. It is written: "And if the זב spits on a pure person." The דרשה: what is in the pure person's hand, I made impure for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and rules it out. A זב's liquids already make vessels impure by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה reads the פסוק to mean that even objects in the hand of the person spat upon become impure. That shows a זב's liquids make vessels impure מדאורייתא. So this case cannot be a rabbinic decree.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with an abnormal discharge, a major source of impurity
spits
a pure person
I (the תורה) have declared impure for you

phrases.english: If you say: through the liquids of a zav
those are Torah law!
as it is written: "And if the zav spits on a pure person"
(meaning:) what is in the pure person's hand, I have made impure for you.
phrases.notes: This דרשה teaches that even vessels he is holding become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible answer to the question in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the case as liquids of a זב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A זב's liquids make vessels impure מדאורייתא, so no decree is needed.

steps.title: It means שרץ-liquids, decreed because of זב-liquids
steps.stepSummary: The case is liquids made impure by a שרץ. By Torah law these cannot make vessels impure, but the רבנן decreed that they do, because of the similar liquids of a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means liquids made impure by a שרץ. This is a decree because of the liquids of a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer. The list means שרץ-liquids touching vessels. The רבנן made this a decree so that people would not confuse these liquids with a זב's liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids made impure by a שרץ are impure מדאורייתא, but by Torah law they are too weak to make a vessel impure. The רבנן gave them that power anyway, because a זב's liquids, which can make vessels impure, look the same.

keyTerms.meaning: liquids of a זב (spit, urine, and the like), a primary source of impurity
a primary source of impurity, strong enough to make vessels impure

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern in this section is consistent. Each item on the list is either deleted (טבול יום) or narrowed to a case that is truly rabbinic. Foods: liquids made impure by hands, decreed because of שרץ-liquids. Vessels: שרץ-liquids, decreed because of זב-liquids.
steps.confusionAlert: שרץ-liquids play two different roles here. For foods, they are the Torah-level case that the decree imitates. For vessels, they are the rabbinic case itself, because by Torah law they cannot make vessels impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that one and the same impure liquid can be Torah-level for one effect (food) and only rabbinic for another (vessels).

phrases.english: Rather, through liquids that became impure because of a creeping creature,
and it is a decree on account of the liquids of a zav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמַשְׁקִין הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ, וּגְזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקִין דְּזָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer to the question in step 8, after step 9 ruled out זב-liquids.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liquids made impure by a שרץ, decreed because of the liquids of a זב.

steps.title: Did the students really make the decree on hands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's claim that the students of שמאי והלל decreed impurity on hands, because שמאי והלל themselves made that decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And hands: did the students of שמאי and הלל make that decree? שמאי and הלל themselves made it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one item in the משנה's list of eighteen decrees: the impurity of hands. It says the decree belongs to שמאי והלל themselves, not to their students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives credit for the decree on hands to the תלמידי שמאי והלל. The גמרא claims the decree is older and came from the masters themselves. The proof for this claim comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Hands. Here it means the rabbinic impurity of unwashed hands, which makes תרומה impure.
The students of שמאי and הלל, meaning בית שמאי and בית הלל
They decreed

phrases.english: And hands: was it the students of Shammai and Hillel who decreed?
Shammai and Hillel themselves decreed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of liquids and vessels to another item in the list of eighteen decrees, which is hands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the students of שמאי והלל decreed impurity on hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source gives the same decree to שמאי והלל themselves, an earlier generation

steps.title: ברייתא listing early decrees, ending with שמאי והלל on hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists decrees made by the early pairs of leaders. The last one is that שמאי והלל decreed impurity on hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה and יוסי בן יוחנן of ירושלים decreed impurity on the land of the nations and on glass vessels. שמעון בן שטח set up the כתובה for a wife and decreed impurity on metal vessels. שמאי and הלל decreed impurity on the hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove its challenge. The ברייתא says clearly that שמאי והלל decreed impurity on hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes through the leaders generation by generation and lists what each one decreed. Its last line names שמאי and הלל, not their students, as the ones who decreed on hands. This seems to contradict our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lands outside ארץ ישראל, which were declared impure
Glass vessels, which can become impure only by rabbinic law
Metal vessels
The marriage contract that protects the wife

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: As it was taught: Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida
and Yosei ben Yochanan of Jerusalem
decreed impurity on the land of the nations
and on glass vessels.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח תִּיקֵּן כְּתוּבָּה לָאִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Shimon ben Shatach instituted the marriage contract for the wife,
and decreed impurity on metal vessels.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁמַּאי וְהִלֵּל גָּזְרוּ טוּמְאָה עַל הַיָּדַיִם!
phrases.english: Shammai and Hillel decreed impurity on the hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That שמאי והלל themselves decreed impurity on hands
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the decrees of the early leaders

steps.title: Proposal: the ברייתא means the groups of שמאי והלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "שמאי והלל" in the ברייתא really means their groups of students. That would match our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the ברייתא means שמאי and his group and הלל and his group,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries an answer: the ברייתא used the masters' names but meant their students. This is only a suggestion, and the גמרא is about to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "שמאי והלל" is a short way of saying their schools, then the ברייתא and the משנה are describing the same decree. There would be no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. This phrase introduces a suggested answer that will soon be rejected.
His group, his followers

phrases.english: And if you say: Shammai and his faction
and Hillel and his faction,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא שַׁמַּאי וְסִיעָתוֹ וְהִלֵּל וְסִיעָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the contradiction between the ברייתא and the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the names in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the decree to the masters personally
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means their schools, the same people as in the משנה

steps.title: Objection: שמאי והלל personally argued only three times
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. The eighteen decrees were made by the students in the middle of disputes, but שמאי and הלל themselves argued in only three places. So the students and the masters are separate groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They decreed eighteen things, and they argued about those eighteen things. Yet הלל and שמאי themselves argued in only three places, as רב הונא said: They argued in three places and no more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion that "שמאי והלל" really means their students. It shows that the masters and the students are clearly separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighteen decrees came with eighteen arguments. Those arguments belong to the students, because שמאי and הלל personally argued only three times. Since the גמרא clearly separates the masters from their schools, a ברייתא that says "שמאי והלל" means the masters themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighteen decrees made on that day in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה
They argued
And no more

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse שמאי and הלל, the people, with בית שמאי and בית הלל, their schools. The schools argued about hundreds of things. The masters themselves argued only three times.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel:
Eighteen matters they decreed,
and about eighteen they disagreed.
Whereas Hillel and Shammai did not disagree
except in three places,
as Rav Huna said:
In three places they disagreed and no more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested answer of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that "שמאי והלל" in the ברייתא means their schools
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The masters and the students are separate groups. The eighteen disputed decrees were the students', since the masters argued only three times.

steps.title: Proposal: masters decreed suspension, students decreed burning
steps.stepSummary: A new answer is suggested. שמאי והלל decreed that תרומה touched by hands is in doubt and must be left alone. Their students made it stricter and decreed that it must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: they (שמאי and הלל) came and decreed that it is held in doubt, and their students came and decreed that it must be burned,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that there were two different decrees, a lighter one and a stricter one. The rejection of this idea comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the masters said the תרומה is "תלויה" (in doubt, so it can be neither eaten nor burned) and the students said "burn it," then both sources are right. Each one describes a different stage of the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave in doubt. The תרומה may not be eaten, but it also may not be burned.
To burn. This is what is done with תרומה that is definitely impure.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵימָא: אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזוּר לִתְלוֹת,
phrases.english: And if you say: they came and decreed to hold it in suspension,
and their students came and decreed to burn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא: אֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזוּר לִתְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 rejected the first answer, this offers a second way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources describe one and the same decree
steps.terutzMaskana: The masters decreed suspension, and the students decreed burning

steps.title: Objection: אילפא says the decree on hands was for burning from the start
steps.stepSummary: אילפא says that from the very beginning, the decree on hands required burning the תרומה. So there was never a lighter first stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אילפא say: Hands, from the beginning, their decree was for burning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the two-stage idea by quoting אילפא. He says the decree on hands was strict from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first decree already required burning, then the masters never had a decree of "suspension." That leaves no room for a softer original version.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of their decree, meaning the original decree
Burning

phrases.english: But didn't Ilfa say:
Hands — the beginning of their decree was for burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer offered in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of a lighter first decree followed by a stricter one
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to אילפא, the original decree already required burning

steps.title: Masters decreed but it was not accepted; students decreed and it was
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: שמאי והלל made the decree, but the people did not accept it. Later their students made the same decree, and the people did accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they came and decreed, but the people did not accept it from them. Their students came and decreed, and the people accepted it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. The same decree was made twice, and only the second time did it take hold among the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sources are true without changing what the decree said. The ברייתא tells us who first made the decree, the masters. The משנה lists it among the students' decrees because their version is the one the people actually accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: They accepted it from them. The people took on the decree in practice.
Rather. This word introduces the answer that replaces the rejected suggestions.

steps.whatToRemember: The decree on hands was made twice. שמאי והלל made it first, but the people did not accept it. Their students made it again, and then it was accepted. That is why the משנה counts it among the students' eighteen decrees.

phrases.english: Rather, they came and decreed
and the people did not accept it from them,
and their students came and decreed
and the people accepted it from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the two rejected answers with a resolution that works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical: the same decree was made twice, and only the second time was it accepted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one group could be the author of the decree
steps.terutzMaskana: The masters decreed first without success, and the students decreed again and were accepted

steps.title: Challenge: שלמה המלך already decreed washing hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: שלמה המלך already made the decree of washing hands, long before שמאי והלל. A בת קול even praised him for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, שלמה decreed it! As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When שלמה set up עירובין and washing of hands, a בת קול came out and said: "My son, if your heart is wise, My heart will be glad, Mine too," and "Be wise, My son, and make My heart glad, so that I can answer those who taunt Me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. If שלמה already made the decree about hands, how can שמאי והלל or their students be the ones who made it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 17 explained the relationship between the masters and the students. But a much earlier source gives the decree to שלמה המלך. So the question of who first made the decree comes back again.

keyTerms.meaning: And still. This word introduces a problem that remains even after the last answer.

phrases.english: And still: Solomon decreed it!
As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
At the time that Solomon instituted
eiruvin and the washing of hands,
a Divine Voice came out and said:
"My son, if your heart is wise,
My heart will be glad, Mine too,"
"Be wise, My son, and make My heart glad,
so that I can answer those who taunt Me!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge even after the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמאי והלל or their students made the decree on hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל teaches that שלמה המלך already set up washing of hands, so it is an older institution

steps.title: The answer to the Solomon challenge begins
steps.stepSummary: The word "אתא" ("came") begins the גמרא's answer to the challenge about שלמה. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the question about שלמה. The full answer continues in the next section of text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אתא" is singular ("he came"), so its subject is most likely שלמה himself, not a later generation. The answer will explain that שלמה's decree had a limited scope and that later sages extended it. The details of how his decree differed from the later ones come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Came. Its subject is שלמה, and it opens the answer explaining what שלמה's decree covered, which later sages then extended.
